text:
The text contrasts two opposing views on human nature. William Golding’s *Lord of the Flies* presents the theme that evil is inherent within humans, illustrated by boys descending into savagery when removed from societal constraints. In contrast, Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s philosophy argues that society is the corrupting force, suggesting that humans are naturally good and free. The similarity lies in both texts addressing the fundamental nature of humanity and the source of moral corruption. The difference lies in their conclusions: Golding sees corruption as internal and innate, while Rousseau sees it as external and imposed by society.

The organ that pumps blood is the heart.
